source_review.notes: Reviewed eight references for ports and adapters, onion structure, information hiding, domain modeling, implementation boundaries, clean dependency structure, enterprise patterns, and architecture quality. Original Cockburn and Palermo articles were checked at their canonical sites; the Parnas DOI resolved to ACM, whose automated client denies content access. The chapter makes durable conceptual claims and no version-sensitive tool claim.

evidence: Reviewed core, inbound-port, outbound-port, driving-adapter, driven-adapter, dependency-kind, allowed-relation, binding, runtime-trace, and obligation-set notation.
Confirmed edge direction, module-set union, prohibited core-adapter edges, binding ownership, and port-obligation terms are defined before use.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation separates static source knowledge, runtime control, configuration binding, and semantic conformance.

numerical_recomputation.notes: The chapter presents no numerical derivation, measured quantity, percentage, or quantitative example.

evidence: Verified the declared relation permits driving-adapter to inbound-port to core and core to outbound-port with driven-adapter depending on the outbound port.
Verified composition binding can select a driven implementation at runtime without adding a core source edge to that implementation.
Confirmed signature equality does not entail satisfaction of ordering, duplicate, timeout, conflict, atomicity, or durability obligations.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The model captures dependency inversion without claiming universal adapter substitutability.

evidence: Reviewed HTTP type leakage, vendor-shaped ports, misleading runtime arrows, weak fakes, remote calls inside transactions, privileged alternate entry, large mappings, service locators, absent sensor values, and safety-relevant device control.
Checked timeout ambiguity, conflicts, duplicates, reentrancy, framework annotations, reflection, plugin discovery, streaming, cancellation, unauthorized adapters, and physical cutoff independence.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Examples cover driving and driven translation, dependency, tests, transactions, security, performance, composition, uncertainty, and high-consequence operation.

evidence: Traced inward dependency, port ownership, runtime/static separation, translation, policy, transaction, substitution, and evidence invariants throughout exposition and exercises.
Confirmed multiple adapters cannot fork authorization, error, concurrency, time, or safety policy silently.
invariant_checking.notes: Core independence is bounded to declared mechanism dependencies and is not presented as deployment, security, or operational isolation.

evidence: Reviewed the runtime/static distinction under dynamic binding supplied by the composition root.
Confirmed the core imports only the outbound port while the concrete adapter imports and implements that port.
Confirmed runtime dispatch reaching the adapter does not introduce a static core-to-adapter source edge.
proof_review.notes: The reasoning applies to the declared binding arrangement and does not rule out hidden reflection, configuration, or shared-data dependencies.

evidence: Audited uses of prove, conformance, independent, atomic, deterministic, faithful, safe, correct, guarantee, and evidence.
Verified fake, mock, contract, integration, composition, and end-to-end evidence remains bounded to its mechanism and environment.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No diagram shape, interface, dependency-injection container, or passing mock test is presented as proof of architectural quality.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter prescribes adapter tests and operational measurements but presents no executed code, benchmark, production trace, or empirical study as reproduced evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed inside/outside policy, hexagonal and onion distinctions, inbound and outbound ports, ownership, domain/application responsibility, driving/driven adapters, translation, frameworks, composition, inversion, transactions, concurrency, security, operations, tests, interface cost, modular composition, limitations, and conformance for coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed provider error mapping, real-adapter contracts, transaction duration, unknown outcomes, identity and authorization, alternate entry points, streaming memory, service location, configuration failure, plugin discovery, telemetry, device timing, and physical safeguards. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified first-principles port/adapter vocabulary, explicit static and runtime models, fifteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in a harbor gate-control transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
